title: How viruses copy themselves
examples: What is the difference between a virus and bacteria?
Can viruses cause diseases in plants?
How fast can a virus copy itself?

explain.say: Viruses need a living cell to reproduce themselves. They cannot make copies on their own.

draw.text: Viruses need host cells to copy.

explain.say: First, the virus must attach to a specific host cell. It looks for a matching receptor.
Next, the virus injects its genetic material into the cell. This is like delivering the blueprint.
Then, the viral genes take over the cell's machinery. They force the cell to copy the viral DNA.
After many copies are made, the new viral pieces assemble inside. They build new virus particles from the parts.
Finally, the new viruses burst out of the cell. This process often breaks the host cell open.

draw.text: Step 5: Burst out of the cell.

faq.a: Scientists do not agree on this. They are often described as being on the border between living and non-living.
asks: Do they need energy to live?

faq.q: What is the difference between viral replication and cell division?
faq.a: Cell division uses the cell's own processes to make copies of itself. Viruses must force the host cell to do the work.
asks: Is it the same as mitosis?

faq.q: How does a virus know which cell to infect?
faq.a: Viruses have specific proteins on their surface. These proteins only fit certain receptors found on the target cell.
asks: Does it need a key and lock?
Can one virus infect many cell types?

faq.q: What does the term 'genome' mean in this context?
faq.a: The genome is the complete set of genetic instructions for the virus. This is usually DNA or sometimes RNA.
asks: Where is the genetic code stored?

faq.q: Why is lysing the host cell sometimes dangerous?
faq.a: When the cell bursts, it releases many viruses at once, which can spread the infection rapidly to nearby cells.
asks: What happens when they burst out?
Is cell death part of the cycle?
Why is the host cell destroyed?

facts: Viruses possess genetic material, which can be DNA or RNA.
The process of making copies of viruses is called replication.
Attachment is the first step, where the virus binds to the host cell.
Lysis is the process where the host cell bursts open.

quiz.say: A virus attaches to a cell using its surface proteins. This step is called:
quiz.why: Attachment is the necessary first step where the virus finds and grips the correct host cell.

wrong.0: Copying happens later when the cell machinery makes new genetic material.
wrong.1: Assembly is the building phase, which happens after the genome has been copied.
wrong.3: Injection happens after attachment, when the viral material enters the cell.

quiz.say: The process where the virus forces the host cell to make many copies of its parts is:
quiz.why: Copying refers to the process where the viral genes are duplicated using the host cell's enzymes.

wrong.0: Assembly is putting the pieces together, not making the copies of the blueprint.
wrong.2: Attaching is only about sticking to the cell surface, not making copies.
wrong.3: Bursting is the final release, not the copying stage itself.

quiz.say: If the virus has finished building many new particles, the next stage is:
quiz.why: The burst stage releases the newly formed viruses, often destroying the host cell in the process.

wrong.1: Injection happens at the beginning, when the virus first enters the cell.
wrong.2: Attachment is the initial sticking process before any internal action occurs.
wrong.3: Copying happens before the final release, making the necessary number of genomes.
